newsitem.title: BOTSWANA: Commonwealth Gold to reopen mine in Botswana.
newsitem.headline: Commonwealth Gold to reopen mine in Botswana.

text.p: Commonwealth Gold Plc (Comgold), due to be listed on the London Alternative Investments Market on March 12, is to reopen Signal Hill gold mine in Botswana, a mine official said on Friday.
The company is also looking at two other sites -- the former New Zealand and Blue Jacket mines -- on its 170 square kilometre lease area.
The mines are 50 km southeast of Francistown on the border with Zimbabwe.
Project manager, Charles Trusscott, said Signal Hill should be in production as an open-cast mine by August and go underground after five years.
"I am expecting to move 25,000 tonnes of ore a month and looking at a recovery rate of two grams per tonne," he said.
Truscott said Signal Hill was last worked in the early 1960s. New Zealand and Blue Jacket were believed to date back to the 1870s.
Signal Hill will toll refine in either South Africa or Zimbabwe. Its operating company will be Sigmor Mines (Pty) Ltd.
